claims.author: ajtowns
claims.harm: reintroducing a generic LogPrint macro conflicts with the existing approach in PR #34038
claims.quote: Concept NACK to reintroducing a generic `LogPrint`.

status_by.quote: This bigger goal of this PR is to replace current implementation of the logging macros which is messy and inconsistent with a clean implementation.

claims.status_note: author explained macro cleanup rationale and proposed supporting NO_RATE_LIMIT flag; reviewer has not replied

claims.author: maflcko
claims.harm: exposing the internal LogPrint macro invites helper patterns that mishandle rate limiting across log levels by silently dropping warnings or errors when info logs overflow
claims.quote: this new macro may encourage to re-introduce helpers of the form: `[](auto level, auto msg) { LogPrint((.level=level),"%s", msg); }`, which will then work incorrectly with regard to rate-limiting

status_by.quote: You give a real place yourself (`WalletLogPrintf`), where a dev (or an LLM) could apply the example today

claims.status_note: reviewer pushed back in rc:2940897215 noting WalletLogPrintf as a real-world example, and author did not reply

claims.author: maflcko
claims.harm: exposing generic LogPrint introduces an alias for level macros, hurting greppability and consistency across the codebase
claims.quote: Just as the logging was fixed to be consistent, so that one can call `git grep LogInfo` to find all info logs, this will introduce a new alias to grep for.

claims.author: cyb3ralbert
claims.question: whether the change in -loglevelalways output omitting category prefixes is intentional, and if help text and release notes should be updated
claims.quote: Is this change intentional? The help text still says "Always prepend a category and level", and the `98f3bd6` commit message says there is no visible effect except in tests.

claims.author: cyb3ralbert
claims.harm: LogDebug accepts invalid flag types such as plain integers or OR-ed masks, which compile but trigger runtime assertion aborts
claims.quote: LogDebug now compiles when passed a plain integer or an OR-ed mask, whereas both failed to compile on the merge-base. For example, `LogDebug(BCLog::NET | BCLog::HTTP, "x")` aborts in a unit test
